name: Texas

sales.rateNote: 6.25% state sales and use tax on retail sales, leases and rentals of most goods and on taxable services. Local jurisdictions can add up to 2%, for a maximum combined rate of 8.25%.

local.levies: cities, counties, special purpose districts and transit authorities
local.capNote: Total local sales and use tax is capped at 2%, so the combined rate never exceeds 8.25%.

groceries.note: Food products such as flour, sugar, bread, milk, eggs, fruit and vegetables are not taxed; soft drinks, candy, beer and wine, and prepared food are taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the August sales tax holiday (items under $100).

otherRates.note: Motor vehicle sales tax of 6.25% of the sales price minus trade-in; new residents pay a flat $90 new resident tax instead of use tax.

holidays2026.name: Emergency Preparation Supplies Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: portable generators under $3,000; certain emergency supplies under $300 (e.g. rescue ladders); batteries, flashlights, portable radios, phone chargers and similar items under $75

holidays2026.name: ENERGY STAR Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: ENERGY STAR air conditioners ($6,000 or less), refrigerators ($2,000 or less), ceiling fans, light bulbs, clothes washers, dishwashers and dehumidifiers

holidays2026.name: Water-Efficient Products Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: WaterSense products and water-conserving items such as rain barrels

sales.holidayNote: Texas also holds an annual back-to-school holiday in August (clothing, footwear, school supplies and backpacks under $100). The Comptroller's page now shows the 2027 dates (Friday, August 6 to Sunday, August 8, 2027); the 2026 dates are no longer displayed.

useTax.note: State use tax at 6.25% plus applicable local use tax on taxable items bought without Texas tax.

facts.text: Texas holds several sales tax holidays a year: emergency supplies in April, ENERGY STAR and water-efficient products on Memorial Day weekend, and back to school in August.
Over-the-counter drugs and medicines with an FDA 'Drug Facts' label are exempt, even without a prescription.
Bakery items are tax-free when sold by a bakery (over 50% of sales from a display case), but taxable elsewhere when sold heated or with utensils.
During the back-to-school holiday the $100 limit applies per item: two $80 shirts both qualify even though the total is $160.
New Texas residents bringing a vehicle registered in their name elsewhere pay a flat $90 instead of 6.25% use tax.

property.levied: local only (school districts, counties, cities, junior colleges and special districts); Texas has no state property tax

assessment.text: County appraisal districts appraise property at market value as of January 1 each year; each local government then sets its own tax rate. Property owners can protest values before the appraisal review board.

homestead.name: Residence Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: School districts must exempt $140,000 of the appraised value of a principal residence (Tax Code 11.13(b)). Any taxing unit may add a local option exemption of up to 20% of value (at least $5,000). A home appraised at $300,000 pays school tax on $160,000.
homestead.applyBy: File Form 50-114 with the county appraisal district; the general deadline for exemptions is before May 1.

otherRelief.name: Age 65 or older / disabled exemption
otherRelief.text: School districts must provide an additional $60,000 exemption; other taxing units may add a local option of at least $3,000.

otherRelief.name: School tax ceiling (freeze) for 65+ and disabled
otherRelief.text: Homeowners receiving the 65+ or disabled exemption have a ceiling on school district taxes; it can transfer to a new home and continues for a surviving spouse aged 55+.

otherRelief.name: Disabled veteran exemptions
otherRelief.text: Partial exemptions of $5,000 to $12,000 by disability rating; a 100% disabled veteran's homestead is totally exempt.

dueDates.text: Property taxes are generally due by January 31 of the following year; unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1 with a 6% penalty plus 1% interest, rising to 12% penalty by July 1.

facts.text: The mandatory school homestead exemption is now $140,000, with an extra $60,000 for owners aged 65+ or disabled ($200,000 in total).
Counties that collect farm-to-market or flood control taxes must give a $3,000 homestead exemption.
Whoever owns the property on January 1 is liable for that year's tax, even if the property is sold later in the year.
If a bill is mailed after January 10, the delinquency date moves so the owner always has at least 21 days to pay.
The Comptroller does not set rates or collect property tax; it runs a biennial School District Property Value Study used for state school funding.

uncertain: Back-to-school holiday 2026 dates are no longer shown by the Comptroller (page updated for 2027: Aug 6-8, 2027); not listed in holidays2026.

The 10% annual cap on homestead appraisal increases (Tax Code 23.23) and the 20% 'circuit breaker' for non-homestead property up to a value limit were not found in readable form on the Comptroller pages; the statute site (statutes.capitol.texas.gov) renders by JavaScript and could not be read with curl.
Date the 6.25% state rate took effect not verified (effectiveSince null).
